summary.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27 domestic grey volumes rose 13.1% with EBITDA of INR5,146 crore and PAT up 17.2% to INR2,604 crore despite a fuel and packing cost shock.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever first quarter across volumes, revenue, EBITDA and profit, with capacity utilisation rising to 81% from 76%. Revenue grew 16%, EBITDA rose 12% and EBITDA per ton held above INR1,200 despite a sharp imported fuel cost increase and packing bag inflation. India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton reaching INR603 from INR509 in the prior quarter, and cables and wires remains on schedule for Q3 FY27 launch. Management guided to a INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27 and reaffirmed double-digit volume growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from INR509 in prior quarter; INR400 earlier; ~INR386 in Q2FY26

financial_highlights.metric: India Cements revenue (ex-factory, net of freight)
financial_highlights.change: +21% vs INR821 crore like-for-like; reported INR1,013 crore vs INR1,021 crore

segments.name: Grey cement (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 13.1%; East slowest in April-June, South and North just under 15%, West and Central above 15%. Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth; industry Q2 growth estimated at 7-8%.

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Brand migration to UltraTech 100% complete; EBITDA per ton INR603 and conversion ratio 1.5x. Cost improvement capex of about INR2,000 crore; green power to rise from ~3% to ~86% by end FY28. Target INR1,000/ton, with full capex benefit from Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Cables and wires
segments.commentary: Investment program INR1,800 crore, with INR888 crore spent or committed. Commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026). Management sees no further investment needed for now.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: RMC is about 3.5% of UltraTech sales; 477 RMC plants. Institutional customers about 35% and retail 65-66% of sales.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 cost increase of INR130-140 per ton, covering fuel, maintenance and monsoon deleverage; packing bags and fuel named as Q1 inflation drivers (fuel +INR25-40/t, bags ~INR9 to ~INR12 per bag).
Management expects Q2 prices to hold broadly steady through monsoon; aims for higher prices but says it will see where it lands.
Targets double-digit grey cement volume growth for FY27; capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by end FY27 and about 235 million tons by March 2028.
Capex of about INR17,000 crore over the next 2-2.5 years; FY26 capex about INR9,500 crore; all growth capex funded by internal accruals; net debt to EBITDA to stay below 1x this year.
India Cements EBITDA per ton target of INR1,000 with full capex benefit from Q4 FY28; INR1,400/ton timeline referenced for Jan-Mar 2028 without war.
India Cements standalone merger path: capex completion and disposal of non-core land, expected Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier.
capex_capacity: Domestic capacity 200.1 million tons after commissioning 8.7 million tons (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu); total capacity 205.5 million tons.
Green power about 1,897 MW (~47% of power needs at quarter end); 71 MW renewables and 19 MW WHRS commissioned in the quarter; target 2.5-3 GW soon.
Cement lead distance down to 360 km from 367 km; AFR substitution ramping up.
Management is drawing up plans beyond 240 million tons; inorganic opportunities to be examined.
Limestone secured for every ton of committed expansion.
demand_pricing: Management cites strong demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate; urbanisation at about 35%, targeted 39% by 2030.
All-India exit prices improved through June; East and South led, Central and West steady, North consistent.
Cost escalations of past two quarters not fully passed through, supporting price outlook into busy season.
Blended cement and premiumisation supporting realisations; converted B/C category customers to UltraTech at higher price points.
Regional: East slowest in Q1 (elections, labour); East expected to see multi-year demand upcycle, not a next-quarter story.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising operating cash flow be deployed across dividends, cement capex and cables and wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Daga said all operating cash flows are fully booked for growth capex plus dividends; no further cables and wires investment foreseen for now, as that business matures first.

qa_highlights.question: What remains before India Cements can be merged into UltraTech standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex programme to be completed and non-core land to be disposed; completion expected Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier, with some operating parameters still to align.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 FY27 cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Jul-Sep quarter, covering fuel, maintenance and operating deleverage; management said it cannot separate war impact from normal seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why did limestone mining cost rise 13-14% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial diesel rose from about INR78-80 pre-war to INR150s during the war, and is a major component of limestone mining cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended coal cost trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended coal cost was USD134/ton in the quarter (INR1.9/kcal); current level about INR2/kcal, with inventory loaded so no further rise assumed. Coal now preferred over pet coke on energy-cost basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook and industry growth for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth; industry growth in the June quarter estimated at 7-8% based on internal intelligence.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption keeping fuel, freight and insurance costs high; Q2 FY27 cost increase of INR130-140/t.
Monsoon dry spells (Rajasthan) could weigh on rural demand and water availability; August-September rains to be watched.
Industry capacity additions may be revisited by some players; industry capacity recalibration pending.
India Cements EBITDA per ton of INR603 still well short of INR1,000 target; benefit from capex only from Q4 FY28.
Cables and wires: higher working capital for the next six months; ramp-up after Q3 FY27 launch.
summary.management_tone: Confident and emphatic on demand, market share and delivery track record, while cautious and non-committal on fuel and war-driven costs ("situation is still fluid"). Management declined to give cables and wires guidance and avoided quantifying some cost questions cleanly, relying on annual comparisons.
key_quotes: We intend to grow like a challenger and not an incumbent.
We absorbed the shock better than any peer, and we will harvest the relief faster than any peer.
We said we will cross 200 million tons; we did a year early.
Our belief is, and we are confident that this year also, we'll end the net debt to EBITDA below 1x.

growth.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 grey volume growth, backed by named capacity coming (200.1 MT domestic now, 212.7 MT by end FY27, ~235 MT by Mar-28) and 81% utilisation, though no explicit revenue growth figure was guided and the Q2 cost increase is a headwind.
